app.name: Shopify Admin API app (own app for Composio)

verdict.summary: Composio has no managed OAuth for Shopify, so you must register your own Shopify app and give Composio its client ID and secret. Setup is quick for a custom app installed on your own development store; a public App Store listing adds review, protected-customer-data approval and token-expiry work.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours for a custom app on a development store (estimate). Add roughly a day for protected-data requests, token-refresh handling and the public review package (estimate).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 1 hour after a Partner account exists (estimate), assuming the scopes you request do not need extra Shopify approval.
verdict.approval_wait: None for a custom app on a development store. For a public app, the documented review window is 5-10 business days (quoted by a community thread); community reports range up to about 30 days during high volume.

gates.name: Development / custom app, works for you
gates.unlocks: You create the app in the Dev Dashboard, set the Composio redirect URL, and connect your own development store through Composio's OAuth flow.
limits: Custom apps cannot be installed on client-transfer stores (f56).
The distribution method cannot be changed once selected (f23).
A declared scope only takes effect after the app version is released and the scope is approved on the store (f12).
gates.time_to_reach: Under 1 hour once a free Partner account exists (estimate).

gates.name: Custom distribution / invited stores (test users)
gates.unlocks: Custom distribution generates an install link you send to a store owner. Protected customer data can be used on development stores once the fields are selected, with no review.
limits: A custom app installs on several stores only when they belong to the same Plus organization (f26).
Protected customer data must be requested before use, including on development stores (f28).
Protected customer fields (name, address, email, phone) must each be requested individually (f30).
Apps that are not approved for protected data get redacted data or errors (f32, f33).
gates.time_to_reach: Same session as Gate 1, plus protected-data field selection in the Partner Dashboard (estimate: under 1 hour).

gates.name: Public app / App Store listing (anyone)
gates.unlocks: Public distribution leads to an App Store listing and review submission, so any merchant can install the app.
limits: Public apps must use expiring offline tokens (f19); all public apps must move to expiring tokens by January 1, 2027 (f20).
Public apps need review for protected-data levels 1 and 2 (f31).
Public apps must be built on the GraphQL Admin API only (f40).
Review can reject an app at Shopify's discretion (f50); failures require resubmission (f49).
gates.time_to_reach: Documented 5-10 business days per review (quoted by community). Reports of about 30 days during high volume. First submissions take longer (community).

steps.title: Decide whether to use your own app
steps.detail: Composio's toolkit record shows no managed OAuth for Shopify, so there is no Composio-owned app to use. You must register your own Shopify app and give Composio its client ID and client secret.
gotchas: Composio's default scope list includes order, customer, draft-order and gift-card scopes. Trim it before you go to review (see the scope notes).

steps.title: Create or sign in to a Partner account
steps.detail: Sign up for a free Shopify Partner account at the Partners page. A Partner account includes unlimited development stores, which you need to test installs before any review.
gotchas: The Distribution card only appears for apps that belong to a Partner organization. Apps built inside a merchant's store organization are installed from the Installs card instead (f24).

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Open the Dev Dashboard and create a new app under your Partner organization. The exact create-form fields were not confirmed by a Shopify page, so follow the on-screen prompts and check the app's Home page afterwards.
gotchas: The Dev Dashboard host returns HTTP 406 to plain GET requests from some tools; use a normal browser session.
The official docs use the Dev Dashboard as the entry point, but older community posts describe the Partner Dashboard for app URL and redirect fields. Check both if a field is missing.

steps.title: Choose the distribution method
steps.detail: On the app's Home page, choose Custom distribution to install on your own store or stores you control, or Public distribution to list in the App Store. Custom distribution gives you an install link to send to the store owner.

values.label: Recommended first choice
values.value: Custom distribution (for development and single-merchant testing)

gotchas: This choice cannot be reversed once made (f23). Pick Custom for testing unless you are sure you want an App Store listing.
Public distribution leads to an App Store listing and review submission (f25).

steps.title: Register the Composio callback as an allowed redirect
steps.detail: In the app's configuration, add the Composio callback URL as an allowed redirection URL. Shopify will not return an authorization code for a redirect URL that is not pre-registered.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect URL must match exactly. Copy it from the Composio auth config, not from older docs.
If the App URL or redirect URLs do not send merchants to the OAuth grant screen, the app will not be approved (f46).

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Copy the app's client ID and client secret from the app's credentials section in the Dev Dashboard. Enter them in Composio's Shopify auth config. The token exchange needs both, plus the one-time code returned on redirect.
gotchas: Never expose the client secret in client-side code or a public repo; the app store rules require that the shared secret is never exposed (f42).

steps.title: Trim the scope list and declare scopes
steps.detail: Start from the Composio default list, then keep only the scopes your agent actually calls. Declare them in the app's version in the Dev Dashboard, then release that version. An agent can draft the scope justification for each scope you keep.
gotchas: Write scopes (for example write_orders) implicitly grant the matching read scope, so you only need to check for the write scope when both are requested (f10).
Declared scopes only take effect after the version is released and the scope is approved on the store (f12).
Reviewers may ask you to prove each scope is required (f41). Use optional scopes for features not every merchant uses (f13).

steps.title: Run a test authorization on a development store
steps.detail: Install the app on a development store from the Dev Dashboard app overview, then connect it through Composio. Confirm the grant screen shows your scopes and that Composio receives a token.
gotchas: A scope that Shopify has not approved for the app fails with missing_shopify_permission: <scope>. Follow Shopify's specific-permission request steps for that scope (f16).
After authorization, check that all required scopes were granted before using the token (f9).

steps.title: Request protected customer data (Gate 2)
steps.detail: In the Partner Dashboard, open Apps, select the app, click API access requests, and request protected customer data. Give reasons and select the protected fields you need (name, address, email and phone must each be requested separately). Complete Data protection details and submit.
gotchas: A Dev Dashboard app's protected-data request still goes through the Partner Dashboard (community report) (f38).
Protected data is requested at the minimum level the app needs. Without approval, GraphQL calls return HTTP 200 with an error in the errors hash (f32, f33).
Orders, draft orders, fulfillments, and customer records all carry protected customer data, which is why several default Composio scopes count (f34, f15).

steps.title: Handle expiring offline tokens
steps.detail: Confirm Composio refreshes tokens; this was not verified in the findings. Shopify's expiring offline tokens last 60 minutes and come with a refresh token. Refresh a few minutes before expiry and again on a 401. Serialize refreshes per shop and store the new token pair together.
gotchas: New public apps created on or after April 1, 2026 must use expiring tokens (f19). Custom apps are not affected by this requirement.
All public apps must move to expiring tokens by January 1, 2027. Merchants do not reinstall (f20).

Refresh tokens last 90 days; a used refresh token can be retried for up to 30 days after first use (f21). An expired refresh token returns 401 and the merchant must reopen the app (community report) (f22).

steps.title: Build the public-listing package (Gate 3)
steps.detail: Draft the listing copy, scope justifications, privacy and data-protection text, and reviewer test notes for the app. Check that the app uses only GraphQL Admin API calls, authenticates with OAuth right after install, and serves every request over valid TLS.
gotchas: Public apps that charge merchants must use Shopify App Pricing or the Shopify Billing API. Off-platform billing keeps the app out of the App Store (f44).
Public apps must authenticate with OAuth immediately after install, before any merchant UI (f39), and must use OAuth on every public app (f45).

steps.title: Record the screencast and set test credentials
steps.detail: Record a demo screencast covering onboarding and features as described in the listing. Create test credentials for the reviewer and set an emergency developer contact in the Partner account.
gotchas: Missing test credentials and broken installs are common review failures (f49).

steps.title: Install and check redirects before submitting
steps.detail: Install the app on a development store from the Dev Dashboard app overview. Check the OAuth redirects and URLs in the Versions page, then confirm merchants reach the OAuth grant screen.
gotchas: The review team only reviews production-ready apps. Apps with errors that block review are not approved (f48).

steps.title: Submit the public app for review
steps.detail: Submit the app for App Store review from the Dev Dashboard. Shopify's Partner Program Agreement and API terms bind you; Shopify may restrict Partner services if they are breached.
gotchas: Shopify may reject an app at its discretion, and requirements can change over time (f50).
Failures for installation, embedding, UI or testing require resubmission (f49).

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: Wait for Shopify's review. Documented window is 5-10 business days (community quote). Each new review cycle after a reviewer is assigned takes about 2-3 business days, and first submissions take longer.
steps.est_time: 1-4 weeks (community reports; up to ~30 days in high volume)
gotchas: If the review window passes 10 business days, one community thread advises contacting Partner Support (community).
A data-protection review is more likely for apps with many installs, many customer records, more approved fields, or long retention (f36).

requirements.item: Own Shopify app credentials (client ID and secret) in Composio
requirements.detail: No managed OAuth is available for Shopify through Composio, so you must register an app and enter its credentials.

requirements.item: Composio callback URL registered as an allowed redirection URL
requirements.detail: Shopify will not return a code for a redirect URL that is not pre-registered in the app configuration.

requirements.item: Distribution method selected on the app Home page
requirements.detail: Required before any protected-data request, including development-store testing. Choice is permanent.
Free Partner accounts include unlimited development stores for testing.

requirements.item: Protected customer data request with reasons and Data protection details
requirements.detail: Submitted in the Partner Dashboard under API access requests. Name, address, email and phone must be requested individually.
Public apps need review for protected-data levels 1 and 2. Apps with name, address, phone or email must meet level 1 and 2 requirements.
Required for new public apps from April 1, 2026 and for all public apps from January 1, 2027. Custom apps are not affected.

requirements.item: GraphQL Admin API only; OAuth right after install; valid TLS
requirements.detail: Rules for public apps listed in Shopify's App Store requirements.

requirements.item: Demo screencast and reviewer test credentials; emergency developer contact
Billing through Shopify App Pricing or Billing API if you charge merchants
requirements.detail: Off-platform billing keeps the app out of the App Store.

scopes.effect: Orders carry protected customer data and need protected-data approval (f34, f15). Orders scopes only reach the last 60 days unless read_all_orders is granted, which requires justification in review (f14). Drop these unless the agent needs orders.
Customer records are protected customer data. Name, address, email and phone fields must each be requested individually (f34, f30). Expect a data-protection review for public apps (f36).
Draft orders carry protected customer data when tied to a customer (f34, f15). Requires protected-data approval.
Fulfillments can contain protected customer fields (f15). Requires protected-data approval if they include customer data.

scopes.scope: gift card, script tag, price rule, discount, marketing event scopes (default list)
scopes.effect: Not individually verified; the full access-scope list was not fetched. Remove any scope the app does not call (f41).
A write scope implicitly grants the matching read scope, so a grant check only needs the write scope when both are requested (f10).
Scopes can be required (granted at install) or optional (requested later and revocable by the merchant). Use optional scopes for features not every merchant uses (f13, f41).

blockers.symptom: Composio shows no managed OAuth option for Shopify; you cannot connect without your own app.
blockers.cause: Composio has no managed OAuth or auth schemes for the Shopify toolkit.
blockers.fix: Create your own Shopify app in the Dev Dashboard and enter its client ID and secret in Composio.

blockers.symptom: Shopify returns an error or no authorization code after the grant screen.
blockers.cause: The redirect URL sent by Composio is not registered as an allowed redirection URL in the Shopify app.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL from your Composio auth config into the app's allowed redirection URLs and retry.

blockers.cause: The requested scope has not been approved for the app on that store.
blockers.fix: Follow Shopify's specific-permission request steps for that scope, or remove the scope from the request.

blockers.symptom: Order, customer or draft-order API calls return redacted data or an error saying the app is not approved for that object.
blockers.cause: Protected customer data is not approved. Without approval, GraphQL returns HTTP 200 with an error in the errors hash.
blockers.fix: Request protected customer data in the Partner Dashboard, select the needed fields individually, and complete Data protection details. On a development store, access works after the fields are selected.
blockers.contact: Partner Dashboard > Apps > API access requests

blockers.symptom: Connections start failing with 401 after about an hour on a public app.
blockers.cause: Expiring offline tokens last 60 minutes. Public apps created on or after April 1, 2026 must use them.
blockers.fix: Confirm Composio refreshes the token a few minutes before expiry and again on 401. Store refreshed token pairs per shop.

blockers.symptom: Public app submission is not approved, or review fails on install, embed or UI issues.
blockers.cause: The app is not production-ready, lacks reviewer test credentials, or does not send merchants to the OAuth grant screen.
blockers.fix: Install on a development store, check redirects and URLs in the Versions page, provide test credentials, and resubmit.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth for Shopify (no managed auth schemes), so you must register your own Shopify app and enter its client ID and secret in Composio. Use the Composio callback URL shown in your Composio auth config as the allowed redirect in your Shopify app. Composio's OAUTH2 entry uses per-shop endpoints under {subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/. Trim the default scope list before review, since order, customer, draft-order, fulfillment and gift-card scopes can reach protected customer data.
